name: stale-seed-defeats-precommit-stat
description: A private-index pre-commit stat is clean BY CONSTRUCTION against its own stale seed, and the update-ref CAS guards the ref not the tree
metadata:

---

A fresh private index plus `read-tree OLD` plus "verify the staged stat lists only your paths"
plus `commit-tree`/`update-ref NEW OLD` can still revert another lane's work, and **both guards
fail silently**. Measured twice in one session (pic-c, AJCR run 0092 r4): commit `4e730419b9`
deleted pic-b's `CurveProjectivity.lean` outright (60 lines) while my stat read exactly
"1 file changed, 160 insertions(+), 27 deletions(-)", my path only.

**Why:** the stat is computed against the same `OLD` the tree was seeded from. A path another
lane advanced *after* your `read-tree` is identical in index-vs-OLD, so it emits no line — the
stat is clean **by construction**, not by safety. And `update-ref OLD NEW` succeeds because
`OLD` genuinely is an ancestor: the CAS protects the *ref*, never the tree's freshness.

**Why:** the two checks people trust are both relative to a snapshot that may be minutes old,
and elapsed time between `read-tree` and `commit` is the entire risk. With many lanes live it
is not fixable by being quick.

**How to apply:** capture `OLD` immediately before `read-tree`, in the same tool call as the
commit. Then *after* committing, run `git show <sha> --numstat` and read every path — that is
the only check that fires. Also verify the commit is **non-empty**: an empty tree means a
sweep already banked your content and your message is detached from any diff, which the
prescribed post-commit `diff HEAD~1 HEAD` displays in a form that reads like success.

[[postcommit-stat-and-head-hash-are-both-needed]], [[commit-stat-names-files-you-never-touched]].
